Sample.evidence_source: An average 6 sessions (range 2–9) were administered over 3.5 months (range 1–5). Children in the NFI group were rated as more compliant. At the end of treatment, 25 CBT subjects (87 percent) and 21 controls (75 percent) did not present any longer with a depressive disorder.

dxgive.evidence_source: At the end of treatment, 25 CBT subjects (87 percent) and 21 controls (75 percent) did not present any longer with a depressive disorder. Ten CBT children (35 percent) and 14 controls (50 percent) still presented with at least one type of psychiatric disorder.
dxgive.warning: The text implies all participants had a depressive disorder at baseline, as it states they 'did not present any longer with a depressive disorder' at post-treatment.

Source.evidence_source: the Self-esteem Inventory (Warr & Jackson, 1983); the Aggression Scale (Olweus, 1978); Children, parents and therapists initially rated their expectancy of improvement; After each session, the therapist rated the child's compliance; Sixteen random treatment sessions were also audio-recorded and rated by an independent assessor; parent-rated MFQ scores
